sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A clustering, fan-leaved palm of moist lowlands in southern Florida, the Caribbean and parts of Central America. Slender stems are 5–7.5 cm thick; plants can reach about 9 m tall with a spread up to 6 m, and leaves about 60 cm across. Small round fruits change from green to orange and then black when ripe.

sections.title: Uses and safety
sections.text: A Florida agriculture factsheet reports that the fruits are edible, without giving preparation or food-safety details. It is also planted as an ornamental.
